title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on the functional equation of L-functions in the geometric case, i.e. over a finite field. Here p denotes the cardinality of the base field, really q. For an ℓ-adic sheaf or motive E on X, with f: X → Spec F_p, the functional equation has the shape L(E, t^{-1}) = δ(E) t^{χ(E)} L(E^∨, t) up to normalisation. Its two constants are:
- χ(E) = Σ(-1)^i rk H^i_c(X, E), the Euler characteristic, which governs the power of t;
- δ(E) = det(-F | RΓ_c(X, E))^{±1}, the constant (ε-)factor, an alternating product of Frobenius determinants.

The page expresses both through the virtual cohomology motives h^i_!(E), the 'virtual components of R^i f_!(E)'. Since χ and δ are additive and multiplicative in exact triangles:
- χ(E) = Σ(-1)^i β_i(E), where β_i are the virtual Betti numbers with coefficients in E;
- δ(E) = Π_i δ(h^i_!(E))^{(-1)^i}.

Grothendieck then invokes the Weil conjectures, implicitly assuming E pure of weight 0 and the situation proper or pure. Frobenius on h^i_!(E) then has β_i eigenvalues of absolute value p^{i/2}, so |det| = p^{iβ_i/2}.

To get δ(h^i) = ε_i p^{iβ_i/2} with ε_i = ±1, he implicitly uses the duality pairing h^i × h^i → Q(-i). This pairing is alternating for i odd and symmetric for i even. Eigenvalues then pair off as α ↔ p^i/α, and real eigenvalues are ±p^{i/2}.
- For i odd, the space is symplectic, so β_i is even and det = p^{iβ_i/2} exactly; hence ε_i = +1.
- For i even, i is even, so iβ_i/2 is an integer in either case. This justifies the 'NB'. The sign ε_i = det/p^{iβ_i/2} is the 'sign of a virtual determinant', the determinant character of an orthogonal similitude.

Conclusion: δ(E) = ε(E) p^{(1/2)Σ(-1)^i iβ_i(E)}, with ε(E) = Π ε_i(E) = ±1 coming only from even degrees. This is the motivic and sheaf-theoretic version of the classical fact that, for X smooth projective of dimension n, Z(X, 1/(q^n t)) = ± q^{nχ/2} t^χ Z(X, t). There the sign comes from the determinant of Frobenius on even-degree cohomology, in practice the middle degree when n is even. The page serves to make the constant of the functional equation explicit.
errors: Implicit hypotheses not stated: purity of weight 0 (to apply Weil's |α| = p^{i/2}) and a self-duality of E (E ≅ E^∨ with an orthogonal pairing). Without self-duality δ(h^i) need not be real, so δ(h^i) = ε_i p^{iβ_i/2} with ε_i = ±1 fails. For odd i, ε_i = +1 needs the alternating pairing.
'p' is used for the cardinality of the base field (should be q in general).

For non-proper X, H^i_c is mixed rather than pure, so 'virtual components' must be understood as weight-graded pieces. The exponent i in p^{i/2} then has to be replaced by the weight. The page glosses over this, though the word 'virtuel' suggests he intends a weight-graded virtual decomposition.

ideas.what: Euler characteristic and constant of the functional equation of L(E,t) expressed additively and multiplicatively through virtual cohomology h^i_!(E)
ideas.modern_name: χ and ε-constant of the Grothendieck–Lefschetz functional equation (global ε-factor over a finite field)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Bourbaki exposé 279, 1964; SGA 5); Deligne (constantes des équations fonctionnelles)
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki Exp. 279 'Formule de Lefschetz et rationalité des fonctions L'; SGA 5

ideas.what: Using Weil purity and duality: det of Frobenius on h^i equals ±p^{iβ_i/2}, with sign +1 in odd degree (symplectic) and integrality of iβ_i/2
ideas.modern_name: sign of the functional equation / determinant of Frobenius on orthogonal (even-degree) cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Weil, Grothendieck); later refined by T. Saito (sign of orthogonal motives via de Rham discriminant, 1994–95)
ideas.where_published: sign ± in Z(X,1/q^n t) = ± q^{nχ/2} t^χ Z(X,t) is in Grothendieck's Bourbaki talk; the explicit ε_i analysis is unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck isolates the sign ε(E) = Π_{i even} ε_i(E), defined as 'signe de déterminant virtuel', as the only non-trivial part of the constant for (self-dual) motives. The page leaves it undetermined. Its computation (via discriminants) was later carried out by T. Saito, not credited to any Grothendieck note.
missed.quote: où ε_i est défini comme un signe de déterminant virtuel, et ε_i est = +1 si i est impair
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor historical interest only: it shows Grothendieck framing the sign problem for orthogonal motives early. The mathematics is now standard (Saito's theorems).

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, correct computation of the constant of the functional equation using Weil purity and duality. Its only interest is that it frames the sign of the functional equation as a 'virtual determinant sign' living in even degrees, anticipating later work on signs of orthogonal motives. Nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Second line probably reads 'On va exprimer δ(E) et χ(E) en termes des [nos] composantes virtuelles...' rather than 'Si on exprime'. The first word is uncertain.
The struck-out symbol before 'f_!(E)' is a crossed-out 'R'. The parenthetical reads '(utilisant conj. de Weil)'.
In the last display, the crossed-out material before ε(E) is a deleted attempt at the same expression. The final text is δ(E) = ε(E) p^{(1/2)Σ_i(-1)^i iβ_i(E)}.
